home.famlin_a_private_family_app: Famlin · A private family app you host yourself
home.famlin_is_young_and_actively: ✨ Famlin is young and actively developed — open source, self-hosted, and shaped by the families using it. Back up your server like you would any home service.
home.a_private_place_for_your: A private place for your family, on a server you own.
home.famlin_is_an_open_source: Famlin is an open-source family app you host yourself. Share photos, milestones, trips and the small everyday stuff with the people who actually care, in plain chronological order. No ads, no recommendations, no company in between.
home.free_and_mit_licensed_ios: Free and MIT-licensed · iOS, Android and web · Source on GitHub
home.your_server_your_data_a: Your server, your dataA home server, a NAS or a small VPS. Photos stay on your disk or your own S3 bucket.
home.invite_only_nobody_finds_you: Invite-onlyNobody finds you by search. People join through a link you send them.
home.newest_first_that_s_it: Newest first, that's itThe feed is in order of posting. Nothing gets boosted or buried.
home.works_for_every_generation_simple: Works for every generationSimple screens, and a web version for anyone who won't install an app.
home.one_app_for_several_families: One app for several families. Grandma can follow both sides of the family in one feed, and still see which family each post came from.
home.post_text_photos_and_videos: Post text, photos and videos to one family or several at once. Everyone can react, comment (with photos of their own) and @mention someone so they get a notification. Big moments like a birthday or a first day of school can be posted as a milestone, so they stand out.
home.save_posts_to_your_favorites: Save posts to your favorites, search older posts, and get an "On this day" reminder of what you shared in earlier years.
home.start_a_trip_with_a: Start a trip with a destination, dates and the people coming along. While you travel, everyone on the trip can check in from each stop with a place name, a note and photos. Back home, the family sees one journal with a day counter and a timeline instead of thirty loose posts.
home.ask_the_family_a_question: Ask the family a question and watch the votes come in: which weekend, which restaurant, which name for the dog.
home.for_the_holidays_start_a: For the holidays, start a gift list. Everyone adds wishes with a link or a photo, and Famlin can run a secret draw (with exclusions, so partners don't get each other). You only ever see who you are buying for.
home.share_a_quick_photo_as: Share a quick photo as a story that disappears after 24 hours, or pin it as a highlight to keep it around. Viewers can react or send you a private reply.
home.each_family_can_also_get: Each family can also get its own group chat for the quick back-and-forth that doesn't need to be a post. An admin turns it on per family.
home.a_smaller_group_inside_a: A smaller group inside a family, like just the grandparents, for posts that aren't for everyone. Members can always see who is in a circle.
home.one_album_the_whole_family: One album the whole family adds photos to, for a wedding, a reunion or a summer at the cottage.
home.link_albums_from_immich_or: Link albums from Immich or a folder on your server, and filter them by person once an admin has matched faces to family members.
home.on_your_phone_tap_share: On your phone, tap Share → Famlin in Photos, Google Photos or WhatsApp and the photo lands in a new post.
home.everything_in_the_browser_on: Everything in the browser on a laptop, with keyboard shortcuts. No install needed, so you can send a link to anyone.
home.heic_from_iphones_works_everywhere: HEIC from iPhones works everywhere, big photos are resized for viewing, and the original is kept on your server.
home.push_and_email_with_a: Push and email, with a switch per type: new posts, comments, reactions, chat, stories, gift lists.
home.any_member_can_download_everything: Any member can download everything they can see as a zip: posts, comments and the photos that go with them.
home.english_dutch_simplified_chinese_europea: English, Dutch, Simplified Chinese, European Portuguese and French. Each person picks their own.
home.running_famlin_for_your_family: Running Famlin for your family should take an evening to set up and a few minutes a month after that. Everything is managed from a web admin panel; you don't need to edit config files after the first start.
home.sign_in_your_way_email: Sign-in your way. Email and password, Sign in with Apple, or any OpenID Connect provider: Google, Microsoft, Authentik, Keycloak and others.
home.families_and_invites_create_families: Families and invites. Create families, send invite links, decide which post types each family can use.
home.your_name_and_colours_give: Your name and colours. Give the app your family's name, logo and colour. The web app and the phone apps pick it up.
home.scheduled_backups_daily_or_weekly: Scheduled backups. Daily or weekly database dumps plus a mirror of all photos, with an email if a backup fails or the disk runs low.
home.storage_where_you_want_it: Storage where you want it. A Docker volume, a NAS share, or any S3-compatible bucket.
home.move_or_restore_in_one: Move or restore in one go. Export everything as one zip, and restore it on a fresh server.
home.moderation_edit_or_remove_posts: Moderation. Edit or remove posts and comments, and resend a notification that didn't arrive.
home.famlin_is_one_docker_container: Famlin is one Docker container plus Postgres. It runs on amd64 and arm64, so a cheap VPS, a Raspberry Pi 4 or 5 or a Synology NAS all work.
home.run_the_installer_on_a: Run the installer on a fresh Debian or Ubuntu server (a few euros a month is plenty). It sets up Docker, HTTPS and automatic updates.
home.open_admin_and_create_the: Open /admin and create the first admin account. Then pick how people sign in.
home.invite_your_family_they_install: Invite your family. They install the app and enter your server's address, or just open it in a browser.
home.on_a_fresh_debian_ubuntu: # on a fresh Debian/Ubuntu server $ curl -fsSL https://famlin.app/install.sh | sh # prefer to read it first? $ curl -fsSLO https://famlin.app/install.sh $ less install.sh && sh install.sh
home.everything_is_written_down_how: Everything is written down: how to install and run a server, how the features work for your family, and how the code fits together if you want to change it.
home.for_the_person_running_the: For the person running the server.
home.for_contributors_and_your_own: For contributors and your own scripts.
home.the_apps_are_free_on: The apps are free. On first launch they ask for your server's address, so the same download works for every family. Prefer the browser? Every Famlin server also serves the full web app at its own address.

privacy.the_short_version_famlin_is: The short version: Famlin is self-hosted, open-source software. Your family's data lives on the server your admin runs — not on any server the Famlin project controls. There's no analytics or tracking built into the app, and nothing is sent back to the project's author.
privacy.1_using_a_famlin_app: 1. Using a Famlin app or server
privacy.a_famlin_server_is_deployed: A Famlin server is deployed and operated by whoever set it up for their family — an "admin." That admin's server stores everything Famlin needs to work: account details (name, email, and either a password hash or your identity provider's subject ID), posts, photos, comments, likes, favorites, group membership, and mobile push notification tokens.
privacy.famlin_s_author_tim_van: Famlin's author (Tim Van Onckelen) does not run, host, or have access to any Famlin server other than for his own family, and has no way to see data from other people's deployments. There is no central Famlin service that instances report back to.
privacy.depending_on_how_your_admin: Depending on how your admin configured the server, the following third parties may be involved:
privacy.your_identity_provider_if_sign: Your identity provider — if sign-in uses OIDC/SSO (Google, Microsoft, Authentik, or another provider your admin configured), that provider processes your login per its own privacy policy. Famlin never sees or stores your password in that case.
privacy.an_email_provider_if_your: An email provider — if your admin configured SMTP, invite and password-reset emails are sent through that provider.
privacy.expo_s_push_notification_service: Expo's push notification service — the mobile app uses Expo to deliver push notifications. Delivering a notification means your device's push token and the notification's minimal content pass through Expo's servers on the way to Apple/Google's push services.
privacy.no_analytics_telemetry_or_crash: No analytics, telemetry, or crash-reporting SDKs are built into Famlin's backend, admin panel, or mobile app.
privacy.deleting_a_post_a_comment: Deleting a post, a comment, or an account removes it permanently — the server erases the row and everything that hangs off it, and there is no restore. You can delete your own account from the app at any time (Profile → Delete account), which removes your profile and all the content you created on that server. Backups, log retention, and any other integrations are entirely up to whoever runs your instance; they're the right person to ask for specifics about your data.
privacy.this_marketing_page_has_no: This marketing page has no accounts, forms, cookies, or analytics of its own. Two things happen automatically when you load it:
privacy.fonts_nunito_jetbrains_mono_are: Fonts (Nunito, JetBrains Mono) are loaded from Google Fonts. That means your browser makes a direct request to fonts.googleapis.com, and Google may process your IP address to serve them — see Google's privacy policy.
privacy.the_site_is_hosted_on: The site is hosted on GitHub Pages, which may log technical request data (like your IP address) to serve the page — see GitHub's privacy statement.
privacy.famlin_is_an_evolving_hobby: Famlin is an evolving hobby project, so this page may change as features change. Meaningful updates will be reflected here with a new "last updated" date.
privacy.famlin_is_a_hobby_project: Famlin is a hobby project by Tim Van Onckelen, not a company — there's no dedicated privacy email. Questions about this policy or the project are best asked via GitHub Discussions or by opening an issue. Questions about a specific Famlin instance and its data should go to that instance's admin.

support.questions_about_the_famlin_app: Questions about the Famlin app, a Famlin server, or the project itself — start here.
support.famlin_is_an_open_source: Famlin is an open-source hobby project, and every channel below is read and answered by the developer, Tim Van Onckelen. Email works for anything and needs no account; the GitHub channels keep the answer where the next person with the same question can find it.
support.the_two_github_links_need: The two GitHub links need a free GitHub account; email does not. Whichever you use, please include which platform you're on (iOS/Android/web), the app version from Profile → App, and what you expected to happen.
support.famlin_is_self_hosted_the: Famlin is self-hosted: the app connects to a server that someone in your family runs, not to a service operated by the Famlin project. That splits support in two.
support.your_family_s_admin_whoever: Your family's admin — whoever set up your server. Ask them about invites, being added to a family, missing posts, someone else's account, or getting your data removed from their server.
support.the_famlin_project_the_links: The Famlin project (the links above) — the app itself: crashes, bugs, something that looks broken on every server, questions about self-hosting, or feature ideas.
support.the_app_asks_for_a: The app asks for a server address. What do I enter?
support.famlin_has_no_central_sign: Famlin has no central sign-up — you need the web address of your family's own Famlin server (something like https://famlin.yourfamily.example). Whoever invited you has it; it's the same address as the invite link they sent. If nobody in your family runs a server yet, one person needs to set one up first — see Self-hosting Famlin.
support.how_do_i_join_my: How do I join my family?
support.your_admin_sends_you_an: Your admin sends you an invite link. Opening it on a phone with the app installed takes you straight into the join screen; opening it in a browser shows the same invite with a download link. Invites expire, so ask for a fresh one if yours has run out. More in Inviting your family.
support.depending_on_how_your_admin: Depending on how your admin configured the server, you can sign in with an email and password, with Sign in with Apple, or with the single-sign-on provider they set up. All available options appear on the login screen once you've entered the server address.
support.ask_your_family_s_admin: Ask your family's admin to reset it from the Famlin admin panel. Because each server is independent, the Famlin project can't reset a password for you.
support.how_do_i_delete_my: How do I delete my account?
support.in_the_app_open_profile: In the app, open Profile → Delete account → Delete my account, then type DELETE to confirm. This is immediate and permanent: your profile, posts, photos, comments, reactions and chat messages are removed from the server, and there is no way to restore them. The same option is in the web app's profile page. If you're the only admin on your server, make someone else an admin first — otherwise nobody could manage it after you leave.
support.check_profile_notifications_in_the: Check Profile → Notifications in the app, and that notifications are allowed for Famlin in your device's system settings. Your admin can also turn push notifications off for the whole server, in which case the toggles are hidden.
support.photos_won_t_upload_or: Photos won't upload, or the app can't reach the server.
support.this_is_almost_always_the: This is almost always the server rather than the app: check whether other family members are affected too, and ask your admin. If it's only you, sign out and back in — and make sure the server address you entered still matches the one they gave you.
support.where_does_my_data_live: Where does my data live, and who can see it?
support.everything_stays_on_your_family: Everything stays on your family's own server. There's no analytics or tracking in the app, and nothing is sent back to the project. See the privacy policy for the details.
